# R4.15e — Signer-key custody per the adopted OQ-170 ruling — signed checkpoints over real keys (DF-S2.5-1, DF-S1.15-1 custody)

Spec: `docs/tickets/164m_R4.15e__signer-key-custody.md` · base `svitali/harnessharness-r4.15d` @ 2279f2b · `live_verification=false` · requirement ids: `OQ-170` (GATE-G7 "Adopt all", 2026-10-22) · `DF-S2.5-1` · `DF-S1.15-1` (custody member) · `R-2.8.6` · `BL-30` · `BL-05` · ADR-0345 trigger (b) · ADR-0359 D2 (scope extension) · ADR-0376 (new — dep-scope ADR).

## Summary

Lands the adopted OQ-170 signer-key custody ruling — checkpoints are
now signed by a **real kernel-held Ed25519 key**, provisioned through
the credential broker, verified by a real resolver, and rotated by a
co-signed checkpoint. `hh-ledger` stays custody-agnostic (the
`AuditSigner`/`AuditKeyResolver` seam only gained algorithm awareness);
`hh-secrets` owns the key material; `hh-embed` wires custody at boot.

- **Custody (`hh-secrets::signer`).** `LedgerSignerCustody` holds one
  Ed25519 keypair per installation as a PKCS#8 document at
  `<store_root>/secrets/ledger-signer.<key_id>.pkcs8`, mode `0600`,
  with the content-derived id
  `ed25519-<hex(sha256(public_key))[..16]>` *in the file name* — a
  renamed or substituted file refuses. `ledger-signer.active` points at
  the active key; multiple keys without it refuse `AmbiguousActive`, a
  pointer at nothing refuses `DanglingActive`. `open` load-at-boot
  returns the active key + every retired key; wrong mode, corrupt or
  unparseable material, mismatched names and malformed ids all answer
  typed `CustodyError` arms — `Ok(None)` only when no key files exist,
  **never** a fabricated/HMAC/env-var fallback.
- **Provisioning is the broker seam.** The `ledger-signer` channel is
  `CredentialKind::SigningKey` — `bindable: false`,
  `AccessClass::KernelOnly`, no destinations, no env projection, no
  canary. `LedgerSignerCustody::install` registers it (idempotent) then
  calls `CredentialBroker::kernel_use(KernelPurpose::LedgerSigning)`:
  the durable `security.credential.used{destination =
  kernel:ledger_signing}` row commits **before** the value returns, and
  the `LedgerSignerKey` is built from that returned value — never a
  file read that bypassed the seam. `CustodySourceResolver` serves only
  `operator_vault:ledger-signer` (active key, mode-checked at resolve)
  and delegates every other coordinate to the host resolver.
- **The ledger verifies real signatures.** `audit.rs` gains
  `ED25519_ALG` + the `<alg>:<hex>` codec — `alg_ref ∈ {hmac-sha256,
  ed25519}` (HMAC retained verbatim), declared length tables (32/64 B),
  `AuditSigner::alg_ref`, `AuditKeyResolver::verify_sig`, and
  `check_checkpoint_signatures` folding the effective signer set.
  `Store::signer_rotation_checkpoint` mints `kind = rotation` rows
  carrying `key_rotation{from_key_id, to_key_id}` — generic
  `checkpoint` refuses the kind — and verification admits the successor
  only when **both** incumbent and successor signed the same unsigned
  claim; retired public keys stay resolvable so historical checkpoints
  keep verifying.
- **Boot wiring (`hh-embed`).** `EmbedService::open` loads custody —
  a defect answers `Refused`, an absent directory stays the honest
  unsigned posture (`signer_key_ids` empty, audit completeness
  `n/a{no signer_key_ids declared}`). With custody present:
  `install_signer_custody` provisions + installs the public-only
  `LedgerSignerResolver` + self-checks (sign-on-boot);
  `RunManifest.signer_key_ids` is **stamped from kernel custody**
  (never caller-declared); `emit_final_checkpoint` writes the
  `kind = final` row at `lifecycle.run.finished` from both the
  post-drive scan and the `close` path (idempotent);
  `rotate_ledger_signer` rotates custody, provisions the successor
  through `kernel_use`, co-signs the rotation checkpoint, and updates
  the resolver in place — the incumbent stays verifiable.
  `set_credential_resolver` composes custody in front of the host
  resolver and re-registers the signer channel.
- **Private bytes cross nothing.** Public key bytes are the only thing
  that leaves custody (the resolver seam); the event stream, manifests,
  child environments, logs and returned audit records are proven clean
  by the batteries below — and `subagent_anchor`/`producer_resolution`
  evaluate against the same installed resolver (real custody, not
  fixture keyrefs).
